title: The 93 'no literal' tasks are not unnameable -- the extractor was wrong

finding.reading: every one of the 93 goals names its target. The executor skipped them because it only looked for QUOTED strings. The 'no literal' class was an EXTRACTOR defect, not a property of the tasks.

two_failed_fixes_kept_in_the_record.why_it_is_wrong: it recovered Click / Create / Book / Keep / Find / Select -- the INSTRUCTION VERBS. A matcher that accepts everything finds the wrong thing (r74). Reporting 93 recovered would have been the largest false claim of the project.

two_failed_fixes_kept_in_the_record.attempt: same extractor + verify the token appears on the page
two_failed_fixes_kept_in_the_record.why_it_is_still_wrong: the survivors were Copy / Draw / Send / Resize / Focus / Generate -- verbs that are ALSO button labels. Appearing on the page does not make a word a target.

the_correct_rule: a target is the object the ACTION is applied to. The verb names the action. Extraction cannot distinguish them by capitalisation or by presence; it must identify the ACTION and exclude it, then take what remains that the page contains.

why_this_matters_for_the_thesis.user_claim: give the model a try in new environments; after once it learns permanently
why_this_matters_for_the_thesis.this_round_supports_it: YES, more than r88 concluded. The targets in this suite are NAMEABLE and PRESENT -- 93 of 93. Nothing here needs semantics that cannot be extracted; it needed a correct extractor.
why_this_matters_for_the_thesis.the_remaining_hard_class: the 7 predicate-referent tasks ('the shortest one'), which r89 showed are solvable by INDUCTION from one demonstration rather than by extraction

honest_status: the extractor is the current bottleneck, not the model and not the router. Three fixes attempted; two produced false positives that would have inflated the number and one produced nothing. The next attempt must be measured against a HELD-OUT set of goals, not the ones used to design it (r69).
